title: Lemma:length / Lemma:apex: 'two-component spanning forest' means an edge subgraph, not a vertex bipartition

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In Lemma:length and Lemma:apex, 'two-component spanning forest {A,B}' must be read as an EDGE subgraph (a pair of subtrees with their edges), not merely a vertex bipartition. This distinction is never made explicit and is a genuine source of ambiguity that affects the counting.

Key fact: the square-flux F_{A,B}(x) = (chi_{A,B}.x)^2 depends ONLY on the cut edge set E(A,B), i.e. only on the vertex bipartition {V(A),V(B)} -- NOT on the internal edges of A,B. Hence many DISTINCT edge-subgraph forests sharing one bipartition all have the SAME flux.

Why this matters and must be addressed:
(1) Lemma:length sums sum_{{A,B}} F_{A,B}(x) over forests. The diagonal-term count uses bijection (a): {forests with e in E(A,B)} <-> {spanning trees containing e}, which is a bijection at the level of EDGE subgraphs (delete e / add e). For the total coefficient of x_e^2 to equal tau, the sum MUST be over edge-subgraph forests, not over vertex bipartitions. If one mistakenly summed over bipartitions the identity tau||x||^2 = sum F + sum C would fail.
(2) In Lemma:apex the target of the injection phi is '{A,B} with F != 0'. The injection phi(R) = {R_ell, R - R_ell} produces a specific EDGE subgraph, and injectivity (Step 3) reconstructs the EDGE SET of R = (A union B) + {f or e}. So '>= tau_e forests with F != 0' must mean >= tau_e edge-subgraph forests. This is correct as written but only because everything is at the edge-subgraph level; the proof should say so.

Concrete illustration (apex multigraph, T = path 0-1-2 with weights (2,4,3), apex v_inf): there are 19 edge-subgraph two-component spanning forests but only 6 distinct vertex bipartitions; tau = 19, tau_e = 6 for the apex edge from v=1, and |v*|^2 = (G_T^{-1})_{11} = 6/19. Lemma:length and the self-pairing both check out numerically ONLY when forests are counted as edge subgraphs.

Fix: add one sentence defining 'two-component spanning forest' as an edge subgraph with two tree components, note F_{A,B} depends only on the bipartition, and confirm phi's outputs are distinct as edge subgraphs (Step 3 already reconstructs the edge set). Also confirm bijections (a),(b),(c) and the matrix-tree count tau = #spanning trees are all at the edge-subgraph level.

Severity: minor (completeness/clarity); the argument is correct under the edge-subgraph reading, which is the intended one. Numerically verified.
